frames.narration: The shared cart holds book x2, pen x1 and lamp x1. The shopper adds a mug on the phone while replica C is down. The write is accepted after 2 of the 3 replicas acknowledge it, which is enough, and replica B keeps a hint to give the mug to C when it returns.
The network now splits replica A from replica B. The phone only reaches A, and it removes the pen. The remove puts a tombstone on the one pen tag it can see, which is A#1.
The laptop only reaches replica B. It removes the lamp and adds one more pen, which gets a new tag, B#7. Both sides accepted a write during the partition, and now each has a different cart.

The partition heals and replica C is back. The stand-in delivers the hinted write, so C has the mug. C is still missing the two changes made during the partition. The next read or the background repair will bring it up to date.
The shopper opens the cart on the laptop. The API reads two replicas. Their vector clocks are concurrent, since each has a change the other has not seen, so neither version simply replaces the other.

The API merges them by uniting the tags and tombstones. The pen tag A#1 is removed, but the new tag B#7 was never seen by that remove, so one pen stays. The lamp stays removed. The mug is present. The result is book x2, mug x1 and pen x1, which nothing was lost from. The merged cart is written back to A and B (read repair).

The shopper checks out. The cart is only a wish list, so checkout takes a snapshot with an idempotency key and moves to the strongly consistent stock and price database, which reserves the items atomically. The mug's price has changed since it was added.

In the background, anti-entropy compares the Merkle tree of the cart's key range on replica A with the one on replica C. The root hashes differ because C still has the old cart, so A sends only the carts under the branches that differ. After that the replicas agree.

messages.label: tree hash differs: send merged cart
